slot.brief: Body under uniform acceleration from rest; distance in the nth second given, find total distance or acceleration.

stem: A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration. The distance travelled by it during the 7th second is 13 m. The distance travelled by it in the first 7 seconds is:

verdicts.working: For uniform acceleration, distance in the 7th second is \(u+\frac a2(2\cdot7-1)=\frac{13a}{2}=13\), so \(a=2\,\text{m/s}^2\). Distance in the first 7 seconds is \(\frac12a(7^2)=49\,\text{m}\).

working:
Distance in nth second from rest = a(2n - 1)/2. For n = 7: 13 = a(13)/2, so a = 2 m/s^2. Total in 7 s = (1/2) a t^2 = (1/2)(2)(7^2) = 49 m.

Independent check: For uniform acceleration, distance in the 7th second is \(u+\frac a2(2\cdot7-1)=\frac{13a}{2}=13\), so \(a=2\,\text{m/s}^2\). Distance in the first 7 seconds is \(\frac12a(7^2)=49\,\text{m}\).
solution: Distance travelled in the $n$th second from rest is $s_n=\frac{a}{2}(2n-1)$. Thus, $13=\frac{13a}{2}$, giving $a=2\,\text{m/s}^2$. $$s_7=\frac12at^2=\frac12(2)(7^2)=49\,\text{m}$$
